The lights were out. A thunderstorm had cut the power. But 8-year-old Tamizh Amudhan had a chess match to play against one of the best players in the world.
By the flicker of a candle, he sat on the floor of his family home in southern India, his laptop balanced on a pillow and its battery draining fast.
Still, the boy played on, pulling off a stunning upset against German grandmaster Vincent Keymer, then ranked world No. 7.
It was the kind of opportunity Tamizh might never have had if his parents hadn’t made a life-changing decision two years earlier.
In 2024, they left behind the stability of life in their hometown and moved to Sivakasi, a small town in India’s Tamil Nadu state, the epicenter of the country’s chess boom. There, they have restructured their lives around one dream: that Tamizh becomes the greatest chess player in the world.

Another day, another sea of placards spilling out onto Europe’s streets.
Protests continued in several European cities on Saturday after tens of thousands filled the continent’s cities on Friday in a youth-led day of action across more than 25 nations.
Student groups in the UK, France, Spain, Italy and beyond walked out on Friday over the sky-rocketing cost of living, rising tuition fees, underfunded education systems and what they cast as leaders’ complicity in Israel’s war in Gaza. In Italy, trade unions also joined the protests and called on their members to observe a nationwide strike.
